grammar.label: intend to (-(으)려고 해요)
grammar.explanation: Use -(으)려고 해요 for a plan you have decided on: 가려고 해요, 먹으려고 해요. It is close to -(으)ㄹ 거예요 but sounds more like an intention.

examples.ko: 이번 여름에 제주도로 여행을 가려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm planning to travel to Jeju Island this summer.
I intend to book the tickets in advance.

grammar.label: before doing (-기 전에)
grammar.explanation: Attach -기 전에 to a verb stem for 'before doing V'. The tense is not added to that verb: 출발하기 전에, 먹기 전에.

examples.en: Before leaving, I look at the map.
Before going to the hotel, I eat dinner.

grammar.label: after doing (-(으)ㄴ 후에)
grammar.explanation: Add -(으)ㄴ 후에 to a verb stem for 'after doing V'. Consonant stems take 은 후에, vowel stems take ㄴ 후에: 먹은 후에, 간 후에.

examples.en: After arriving at the hotel, I unpack.
After eating, I take a walk.

grammar.label: let's (-(으)ㅂ시다)
grammar.explanation: -(으)ㅂ시다 means 'let's', neutral and slightly written. Use it for a group plan; -(으)ㄹ까요? is the softer, more conversational suggestion.

words.en: was fun, had a good time

sentences.korean: 이번 여름에 제주도로 여행을 가려고 해요.
sentences.romanization: ibeon yeoreume jejudo-ro yeohaengeul garyeogo haeyo.
sentences.english: I'm planning to travel to Jeju Island this summer.
sentences.literal: This summer, to Jeju Island, travel go-intend.
distractors: I'm planning to travel to Jeju Island this winter.
I traveled to Jeju Island this summer.
I'm not planning to travel to Jeju Island.
sentences.notes: 도 takes 로 when it ends in a vowel: 제주도 → 제주도로.

sentences.english: I'm planning to go to Busan by train.
sentences.literal: As far as Busan, by train go-intend.
distractors: I'm planning to go to Busan by plane.
I went to Busan by train.
I'm planning to go to Daegu by train.
sentences.notes: 까지 marks the end point of the journey; 로 marks the means.

sentences.english: I intend to book the plane tickets in advance.
sentences.literal: Plane tickets in advance reserve-intend.
distractors: I intend to book the train tickets in advance.
I booked the plane tickets in advance.
I don't intend to book the plane tickets.
sentences.notes: 예약하다 + 려고 해요 → 예약하려고 해요. The 려 goes straight onto 하.

sentences.korean: 짐이 많아서 공항에 일찍 가려고 해요.
sentences.romanization: jimi manaseo gonghange iljjik garyeogo haeyo.
sentences.english: I have a lot of luggage, so I'm planning to go to the airport early.
sentences.literal: Luggage is-much-because, to the airport early go-intend.
distractors: I have a lot of luggage, so I'm planning to go to the airport late.
I have little luggage, so I'm planning to go to the airport early.
I have a lot of luggage, so I'm planning to go to the hotel early.
sentences.notes: The reason clause comes first, then the intention at the end.

sentences.english: I'm going to put my passport in my bag.
sentences.literal: Passport in-bag put-in-intend.
distractors: I'm going to put my ticket in my bag.
I'm going to take my passport out of my bag.
I put my passport in my bag.
sentences.notes: 넣다 has a ㅎ final, so it takes 으려고: 넣 + 으려고.

sentences.english: We're planning to set the travel schedule together.
sentences.literal: Travel schedule together decide-intend.
distractors: We're planning to cancel the travel schedule.
We set the travel schedule together.
We're planning to set the travel schedule alone.
sentences.notes: Korean does not need a subject here; 함께/같이 makes it 'we' in feel.

sentences.english: Before leaving, I look at the map.
sentences.literal: Before departing, the map look-at.
distractors: After leaving, I look at the map.
Before leaving, I buy a map.
Before arriving, I look at the map.
sentences.notes: -기 전에 attaches to the stem with no tense: 출발하 + 기 전에.

sentences.english: After arriving at the hotel, I unpack my luggage.
sentences.literal: After arriving at the hotel, luggage untie.
distractors: Before arriving at the hotel, I unpack my luggage.
After arriving at the hotel, I pack my luggage.
After arriving at the airport, I unpack my luggage.
sentences.notes: 도착하다 ends in a vowel, so it takes ㄴ: 도착한 후에.

sentences.korean: 점심에 해산물을 먹은 후에 관광을 해요.
sentences.romanization: jeomsime haesanmureul meogeun hue gwangwangeul haeyo.
sentences.english: After eating seafood for lunch, I go sightseeing.
sentences.literal: At lunch seafood eat-after, sightseeing do.
distractors: Before eating seafood for lunch, I go sightseeing.
After eating seafood for dinner, I go sightseeing.
After eating seafood for lunch, I go back to the hotel.
sentences.notes: 먹다 has a consonant stem, so it takes 은: 먹은 후에.

sentences.english: Before seeing the night view, I look around the sea.
sentences.literal: Before seeing the night view, the sea look-around.
distractors: After seeing the night view, I look around the sea.
Before seeing the sunrise, I look around the sea.
Before seeing the night view, I go back to the hotel.
sentences.notes: 구경하다 is for looking around a place or a sight; 보다 is for watching something specific.

sentences.english: Before going to the museum, I buy a ticket.
sentences.literal: Before going to the museum, a ticket buy.
distractors: After going to the museum, I buy a ticket.
Before going to the museum, I buy a map.
Before going to the beach, I buy a ticket.
sentences.notes: -기 전에 can follow a movement verb as well: 가기 전에 = before going.

sentences.english: After buying souvenirs, I go to the beach.
sentences.literal: After buying souvenirs, to the beach go.
distractors: Before buying souvenirs, I go to the beach.
After buying souvenirs, I go to the museum.
After buying tickets, I go to the beach.
sentences.notes: 사다 is irregular here: 사 + ㄴ = 산, so 산 후에 = after buying.

sentences.english: After booking the tickets, I pack my luggage.
sentences.literal: After booking tickets, luggage pack.
distractors: Before booking the tickets, I pack my luggage.
After booking the tickets, I unpack my luggage.
After booking the hotel, I pack my luggage.
sentences.notes: 예매하다 is the usual verb for booking tickets in advance; 예약하다 is for rooms and tables.

sentences.english: Before going to Haeundae, I decide on the accommodation.
sentences.literal: Before going to Haeundae, accommodation decide.
distractors: After going to Haeundae, I decide on the accommodation.
Before going to Haeundae, I decide on the airline.
Before going to the museum, I decide on the accommodation.
sentences.notes: 정하다 is 'to decide on'; 숙소를 정하다 = book/choose where to stay.

sentences.english: After renting a car, I go to the beach.
sentences.literal: After renting a rental car, to the beach go.
distractors: Before renting a car, I go to the beach.
After renting a car, I go to the museum.
After buying a car, I go to the beach.
sentences.notes: 빌리다 ends in a vowel, so it takes ㄴ: 빌린 후에.

sentences.romanization: yeohangsaseo ilbak iil yeohaengeul yeyakharyeogo haeyo.
sentences.english: I'm planning to book a two-day trip at the travel agency.
sentences.literal: At the travel agency, one-night-two-day trip reserve-intend.

gloss.en: a one night, two day trip (object)

distractors: I'm planning to book a three-day trip at the travel agency.
I booked a two-day trip at the travel agency.
I'm planning to book a two-day trip at the hotel.
sentences.notes: 1박 2일 is read 일박 이일: one night, two days.

sentences.english: Let's go to the museum with the guide.
sentences.literal: With the guide together, to the museum let's-go.
distractors: Let's go to the museum without the guide.
Let's go to the beach with the guide.
We went to the museum with the guide.
sentences.notes: 가다 + ㅂ시다 = 갑시다. The ㅂ is written as ㅂ before 시다.

sentences.english: I'm planning to come to Busan again next time.
sentences.literal: Next time, again to Busan come-intend.
distractors: I'm planning to come to Busan again tomorrow.
I came to Busan again last time.
I'm not planning to come to Busan again.
sentences.notes: 오다 is 'come' from the listener's side - here the speaker is already in Busan.

sentences.english: On the first day, I'm planning to watch the sunrise.
sentences.literal: On the first day, sunrise see-intend.
distractors: On the first day, I'm planning to watch the sunset.
On the last day, I'm planning to watch the sunrise.
On the first day, I watched the sunrise.
sentences.notes: 보다 + 려고 → 보려고. No ㄹ is added before 려.

sentences.english: I'm planning to take a boat to the island.
sentences.literal: A boat ride-and, to the island go-intend.
distractors: I'm planning to take a bus to the island.
I'm planning to take a boat to the beach.
I took a boat to the island.
sentences.notes: 배를 타고 = ride a boat and…; 타다 is used for boats, buses and bikes.

sentences.english: After arriving on the island, I look around at the scenery.
sentences.literal: After arriving at the island, scenery look-around.
distractors: Before arriving on the island, I look around at the scenery.
After arriving on the island, I go to the museum.
After arriving at the airport, I look around at the scenery.
sentences.notes: 풍경 is the view or scenery itself; 구경 is the act of looking around.

sentences.english: On the last day, I'm planning to watch the sunset.
sentences.literal: On the last day, sunset-glow see-intend.
distractors: On the last day, I'm planning to watch the sunrise.
On the first day, I'm planning to watch the sunset.
On the last day, I watched the sunset.
sentences.notes: 노을 is the red glow at sunset; 일출 is the sunrise event.

sentences.english: After checking in, I'm planning to rest in the room.
sentences.literal: After check-in, in the room rest-intend.
distractors: Before checking in, I'm planning to rest in the room.
After checking out, I'm planning to rest in the room.
After checking in, I'm planning to go to the beach.
sentences.notes: 쉬다 + 려고 → 쉬려고. Two endings can stack: 체크인한 후에 … 쉬려고 해요.

sentences.english: Let's look at the view before checking out.
sentences.literal: Before checking out, the view let's-look.
distractors: Let's look at the view after checking out.
Let's check out before looking at the view.
I looked at the view before checking out.
sentences.notes: 보다 + ㅂ시다 = 봅시다. -(으)ㅂ시다 includes the speaker, so it fits a group plan.

reading.title: Two days in Busan
reading.ko: 금요일 저녁에 부산에 도착했어요. 숙소는 해운대 근처였어요. 조용하고 편했어요. 토요일 아침에 일찍 일어나서 해변을 걸었어요. 날씨가 따뜻했어요. 점심에는 유명한 식당에서 해산물을 먹었어요. 아주 맛있었어요. 오후에는 배를 타고 섬에 갔어요. 섬의 풍경이 정말 좋았어요. 저녁에는 노을을 봤어요. 마지막 날에는 시장에서 기념품을 샀어요. 사람들이 친절했어요. 1박 2일은 조금 아쉬웠어요. 그래도 아주 즐거웠어요. 일요일 저녁에 서울로 돌아왔어요. 다음에 또 가고 싶어요.
reading.en: I arrived in Busan on Friday evening. The accommodation was near Haeundae. It was quiet and comfortable. On Saturday morning I got up early and walked along the beach. The weather was warm. For lunch I ate seafood at a famous restaurant. It was delicious. In the afternoon I took a boat to an island. The scenery on the island was really good. In the evening I watched the sunset. On the last day I bought souvenirs at the market. The people were kind. Two days was a bit of a shame. Still, it was a lot of fun. I came back to Seoul on Sunday evening. I want to go again next time.

questions.q: When did the writer arrive in Busan?
questions.why: 금요일 저녁에 부산에 도착했어요 = I arrived in Busan on Friday evening.

questions.q: What did the writer do on Saturday morning?
options: Took a boat to an island
questions.why: 토요일 아침에 일찍 일어나서 해변을 걸었어요.

questions.q: How did the writer feel about the trip?
options: It was fun but too short
